findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable through instance metadata and EC2 APIs by principals with instance-description access, exposing the database credential beyond a dedicated secrets store.

`publicly_accessible = true` assigns the RDS instance a public network address. Although the shown security group limits MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to public-network reachability and makes later security-group changes more dangerous.

`storage_encrypted = false` leaves RDS database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and read replicas unencrypted at rest. Compromise of underlying storage or snapshot access can expose database contents.
This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to `0.0.0.0/0`. It creates an unnecessary exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database network interface.

The EC2 instance role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. A compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would allow broad account-wide data access and infrastructure control, including potential privilege-escalation paths.

No `metadata_options` configuration requires IMDSv2, so the instance permits IMDSv1 by default. An SSRF flaw in the web application could retrieve the highly privileged instance-role credentials without an IMDSv2 session token.
